sections.content: You know this from Unit 12. *Hová?* (“where to?”) asks where someone is going, and the place answers with *-ba* or *-be*: the same ending with the *-n* dropped. *A boltba megyek.* The vowel rule is the same as before, and a final *-a* still grows long: *iskola* becomes *iskolába*. The verb for going is *megy*: *megyek* (I), *mész* (you), *megy* (he, she, Anna). *Hová* can also be written *hova*.

sections.title: Choosing the set
sections.content: The question decides. *Hol?* goes with *-ban/-ben* and *vagyok, vagy, van*. *Hová?* goes with *-ba/-be* and *megyek, mész, megy*. To say no, put *nem* right before the verb: *Nem megyek az irodába.* To name the other place, put *nem* before the place: *Nem a boltba megyek, a parkba megyek.*

items.english: I am going to the park.
Anna is not going to the office.

sections.content: Compare *a konyhában* (“in the kitchen”) with *a konyhába* (“into the kitchen”): one letter decides whether you stay or go. Never mix the sets: *A kertbe vagyok* is wrong, and *A kertben megyek* does not say where you are going. *Haza* (“home”, as a direction) and *otthon* (“at home”) take no ending.
